name: Mairang
description: District headquarters of Eastern West Khasi Hills, a historic hill town about 40 km from Shillong on the route to Nongstoin. Known as the home of freedom fighter U Tirot Sing Syiem and as a base for exploring Kyllang Rock, valleys, and Khasi cultural sites.
facts: Headquarters of Eastern West Khasi Hills district (created 2021)
About 40 km from Shillong along NH-106
Elevation around 1,564 metres
Associated with U Tirot Sing and Anglo-Khasi War

name: Kyllang Rock
description: Massive granite monolith dome rising about 1,774 m (5,820 ft), located roughly 9-12 km northwest of Mairang. Steeped in Khasi folklore as a personified figure who battled Symper Rock; offers panoramic views after a short climb, with rare white rhododendrons nearby.
facts: Large granitic dome about 1,000 feet wide
Accessible from northern and eastern flanks
Linked to Khasi legends of battle with Symper Rock
About 60 km from Shillong

name: Mawthadraishan Peak
description: Highest point in Eastern West Khasi Hills at 1,924.5 metres (6,314 ft), midway between Mairang and Nongstoin. Offers 360-degree panoramic views of the Khasi Hills, Garo Hills, and distant Himalayas on clear days, with natural ponds on the range.
facts: Highest elevation in the district at 1,924.5 m
Located on the Mawthadraishan Range
About 70 km from Shillong
Views of Assam plains and Himalayas post-monsoon

name: Ka Phan Nonglait Falls
description: Serene waterfall near Mairang, named after the unsung Khasi woman warrior Phan Nonglait who aided U Tirot Sing against the British by disarming soldiers at the falls during the Anglo-Khasi War. Surrounded by lush forests.
facts: Named after female freedom fighter Phan Nonglait
About 10 km from Mairang
Site linked to events of the Anglo-Khasi War
Peaceful setting amid forests

name: Tirot Sing Ecological Park
description: Park in Mairangbah village featuring a statue of U Tirot Sing, an old colonial-era pine tree, children's play area, and views of sunrise and sunset over Mairang town. Combines history, recreation, and local culture.
facts: Located at Mairangbah village
Features statue of freedom fighter U Tirot Sing
Colonial-period pine tree as attraction
Good sunrise and sunset views of the town

name: Markham and Remkhla Valley
description: Rolling green hills and valleys near Markham and Mawkyllei villages, locally known as Laitmurok viewpoint. Famous for misty mornings, grassland meadows, and scenic rural landscapes; often compared to a mini Dzukou Valley.
facts: Situated near Markham and Mawkyllei villages
Known for unique beauty and grazing lands
Border area with South West Khasi Hills
Emerging offbeat destination for nature lovers

name: Laitarted Lake
description: Popular tourist attraction lake in Eastern West Khasi Hills, offering a peaceful natural setting amid the hills for visitors seeking quiet outdoor experiences.
facts: Listed among popular attractions of the district
Scenic natural setting
Accessible from district headquarters

name: Kynshi River (Eastern West Khasi Hills section)
description: Major river coursing through Eastern West Khasi Hills with tributaries featuring rapids, waterfalls, and stunning riverine terrain. Enhanced by silver reeds in season; popular for scenic views and potential adventure.
facts: Flows as an artery through the district
Features mighty rapids and waterfalls
Silver reeds enhance beauty seasonally
Part of the broader Kynshi river system
